policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for N times' (two, three, ...) means N pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the position of the cube that the demonstration picked up, derived from the demonstration steps at the first decision step and tracked through the shuffle swaps). Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - If the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%), the robot is holding the cube, regardless of the table list (the held cube is usually still listed at its old position): choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open; the robot holds nothing even if a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table', which is a cube just released and settling): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube as updated at this step (after a put-down this is the current position of the cube the execution steps showed released); if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. If a situation matches no rule (for example the gripper state is ambiguous or target_cube cannot be matched to any listed cube), prefer: holding something -> B; not holding and picks_done below the requirement -> A at the cube nearest target_cube; else -> C. Always point at target_cube as updated at this step.

fields.name: target_cube
fields.description: Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked, at its current table position. At the first decision step (memory empty), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS: find the frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%; the picked cube is the cube listed nearest the gripper's own [y, x] there (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames confirms it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). Then follow that cube's identity through every later demonstration frame, including the shuffle, by matching each cube to its nearest position in the previous frame; when two cubes move at once they are exchanging places, so the picked cube ends where its arc ends, not where it started (two swaps of the same pair put it back). Write its position in the scene at the start of execution. At every later decision step: if the execution steps shown contain a cube 'held in the gripper' that is then released (fingers reopen to 100% at height about 0.02), write that cube's position in the scene at this decision step; otherwise write the position of the listed cube within about 10 px of the carried value, or copy the carried value if none is listed. Ignore 'lifted off the table' lines. e.g. [85, 109]

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of completed grasps. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, write the carried value plus one if the execution steps shown include a frame with the gripper at about height 0.02 and fingers going from 100% to about 46% (or any 'is held in the gripper' line) AND the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers about 46% open (not 100%). Do not require the cube to be missing from the table list; it is usually still listed at its old position. Otherwise, and always when the fingers at the scene are 100% open (even if a cube is listed 'lifted off the table'), copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. 2
